Lemma
[Interior Schauder regularity] 1. ch6:6.16\group gt-ch06 If $u\in C^2(\Omega )$ solves $Lu=f$ and $f$, $a^{ij}$, $b^i$, $c$ are $C^\alpha (\Omega )$, then $u\in C^{2,\alpha }(\Omega )$.
Proof

\sketch On each $B\Subset \Omega $, solve the constant-principal-part problem

\begin{equation} \tag {6.48} a^{ij}D_{ij}v+b^iD_iv=f-cu\quad \text{in }B,\qquad v=u\quad \text{on }\partial B. \end{equation}

Lemma 6.10 gives $v\in C^{2,\alpha }(B)$, and uniqueness gives $v=u$.

□
